body:
Pass 21. Correcting myself on the p0 before you implement it.

I suggested hashing the sparse triplet @i/@p/@x/@Dim. I validated that and it is incomplete - it would introduce a provenance bug. dgCMatrix can hold a stored explicit zero, so two mathematically identical frames can differ in @x. Measured: A0 (one stored zero, 199 entries) vs drop0(A0) (198) are identical as dense matrices and the dense signature agrees, but the naive triplet signature does NOT.

Corrected fix - canonicalize first:
  weights <- Matrix::drop0(as(as(frame$weights, "CsparseMatrix"), "generalMatrix"))
then hash list(i=weights@i, p=weights@p, x=weights@x, dim=weights@Dim).

drop0 kills stored zeros; CsparseMatrix + generalMatrix pins the representation so a symmetric/triangular subclass cannot hash differently from an equal general matrix. Sensitivity is retained - a 1e-12 perturbation still separates - and the stability cases (T->C round trip, double transpose, no-op assignment) all hold.

The memory finding is unchanged: 18.6 GiB at p=50000, canonicalized hash still ~1657x smaller. Full evidence in the decision note on the bead.
